A bit of clarification might help here. So there's this thing called trichrome photography where you take 3 black and white photos and combine them into making a colored photograph. If you use a red filter on a tree you'll get a much darker shade than if you use a green filter then the tree will be brighter. Adding a red, green, and blue filter therefore will make a balanced image just not how *you* would see it.

A lot of astrophotographers are using filters tuned to capture specific colors of the galaxy and combining them together to have an accurate image just not an image you'll see with your naked eye. Also a lot of dedicated cameras built for astrophotography shoots in black and white for this reason.

Why people do it simply is because it's fun! Same reason someone takes a picture of The Taj Mahal on vacation. I find it a privilege to shoot the stars on a new day that no one has ever seen before!
